Synopsis:
European crop maturity and harvest dates have shifted significantly earlier due to accelerating climate change, with winter wheat, rapeseed and maize now maturing up to 20 days sooner than in 2000. Repeated 2026 heatwaves from late May compounded the structural warming trend. Beyond earlier timing, crop quality and yields are severely impacted: French grain maize condition is at its worst on record (27% good/excellent), with France's agriculture ministry forecasting a 35% production drop YoY, while analysts project a near-50% collapse to the lowest output since 1976.
